paths.name: @copilotkit/react-core
paths.message: The legacy root entry point is restricted WHOLE: it exports executable registrants (useFrontendTool, useHumanInTheLoop, useCopilotAction, useDefaultTool, useCopilotAuthenticatedAction_c), the legacy action registry (CopilotContext, useCopilotContext), an executable task runner (CopilotTask), a HITL resume handler (useLangGraphInterrupt) and the legacy provider (CopilotKit) -- and it re-exports more through wildcards. Production imports nothing from it, so the whole specifier is closed rather than enumerated. Use components/ai/register-model-visible-tool.ts, copilotkit-core-access.ts and assistant-copilot-provider.tsx.

paths.name: @copilotkit/react-core/v2
paths.message: Each of these executes or resumes a model-callable handler, or yields a core that can register one -- including CopilotKitCore and RunHandler, which reach this specifier through its `export * from "@copilotkit/core"` wildcard and expose addTool/removeTool/setTools/setToolEnabled/runTool. Register through useModelVisibleTool, obtain per-turn runtime through copilotkit-core-access.ts, and mount the provider through assistant-copilot-provider.tsx. Renderer-only hooks (useRenderTool, useRenderToolCall, useDefaultRenderTool, defineToolCallRenderer) are deliberately NOT restricted: they add a ReactToolCallRenderer and cannot register, replace or respond with an executable result.

paths.name: @copilotkit/react-core/v2/context
paths.message: This subpath publicly exports useCopilotKit, CopilotKitContext and the CopilotKitCoreReact class, so any of them yields the live mutable core. Read core configuration through components/ai/copilotkit-core-access.ts instead. The whole specifier is restricted because every one of its exports is a route to the same capability.

paths.name: @copilotkit/react-core/v2/headless
paths.message: The headless entry point is restricted WHOLE: it exports executable registrants (useFrontendTool, useHumanInTheLoop, useComponent), a HITL resume handler (useInterrupt), core access (useCopilotKit, CopilotKitCoreReact) and the same `export *` wildcards as /v2, which carry CopilotKitCore and RunHandler. Production imports nothing from it, so the whole specifier is closed rather than enumerated.

paths.name: zundo
paths.message: The temporal middleware is retired. Undo/redo is a durable repository operation (scenarioCommands.undo/redo) whose availability is read from the committed envelope, not a per-tab in-memory stack that lies across tabs.

paths.name: zustand/middleware
paths.message: The scenario projection is no longer a persist-wrapped store. Durable writes go through the repository transaction and are PUBLISHED into the projection afterwards; a write-behind would put the view ahead of the commit again, which is the exact failure the T03 cutover removed.

paths.name: lucide-react
paths.message: The project standardizes on react-icons Font Awesome 6 (react-icons/fa6), re-exported through components/icons.tsx. lucide-react arrives as a transitive shadcn/base-nova dependency and is not this app's icon set: importing it would put two icon families -- two stroke weights, two optical sizes -- on the same screen. Migrated here from the recursive app/ + components/ source walk in app/design-system.test.ts, which is exactly the job no-restricted-imports already does natively.

paths.name: @copilotkit/react-core/v2/styles.css
paths.message: The CopilotKit v2 stylesheet is a PRODUCTION CSS ENTRY and there is exactly one: `app/layout.tsx`, which imports it before `./globals.css` so the token mapping in globals.css can re-point the library's scoped theme. A second entry double-ships ~87KB and, if it lands after globals.css, silently undoes that mapping and returns the dock to the library's pure-white / near-black defaults. This restriction replaces the recursive app/ + components/ import walk that components/ai/assistant-styles.test.ts used to run: closing the specifier makes a second entry UNAVAILABLE rather than merely unspelled, and unlike the walk it covers aliases, re-export chains and dynamic import() in every directory. Whether the sheet is actually shipped and ACTIVE is owned by e2e/ai-assistant-chat-ui.spec.ts against a real production build.

patterns.message: The CopilotKit RUNTIME is reachable only through lib/ai/runtime/copilotkit-runtime.ts, which applies the telemetry/analytics containment env before the package's telemetry singleton snapshots it. Importing the package anywhere else boots an uncontained runtime and breaks the single-instance identity Phase 1 depends on.

The durable repository is reached only by the projection adapter (lib/store/authority.ts) and the explicitly listed modules that own their own tables or the write fence. Everything else changes durable scenario state through scenarioCommands / assistantProposalCommands, so a failed write can never leave the view showing something that was not saved.
Same boundary as the aliased specifier: a RELATIVE path into lib/repository is the same crossing. This regex is why the boundary is not merely a spelling rule about `@/lib/repository`.

AI IS OPTIONAL. With the feature off, no key stored, or OpenRouter unreachable, every manual workflow and ordinary Optimize keeps working -- and what guarantees that is that no scheduling code DEPENDS on assistant code. The assistant's modules may be imported by itself, its UI, the settings card, the two shell surfaces that mount it (both render null until it is Ready), the same-origin AI routes, and the boot instrumentation. Every one of those is listed by name in an override, because a new entry is a deliberate widening of the seam.
Same boundary, relative spelling: a path into lib/ai or components/ai crosses it whichever way it is written.

The module does not exist, so the compiler already refuses this import -- this rule is what makes the refusal say why.

Test and support code may not acquire a compiler or parser library. Every guarantee that used to be proved by parsing authored source now sits at the first layer that can own it honestly: a production API, a TypeScript option or negative fixture, an Oxlint restriction, a runtime/behavioural test, or a declarative ast-grep rule with its own valid/invalid fixtures. THIS FAMILY HAS NO AUDITED EXCEPTION ANYWHERE -- if a guarantee appears to need a parser, the answer is to change the production API, not to import one here. This rule owns every literal specifier for these packages, static and dynamic alike; ast-grep owns only the residual `require()` / `createRequire` / `getBuiltinModule` call shapes, in which no specifier appears for an import rule to see.

Generic filesystem capability is not available to test/support code. Readers are granted to an exact FILE, never to a directory glob, and every one is recorded with its API, root/path class, extension/format and write permission in the reader ledger. If this file genuinely needs a fixture, add it to the ledger with a justification and reviewer approval and it gets an exact override -- but a file that opens a production .ts/.tsx for its CONTENTS gets none, and neither does a known source analyzer. Prefer a format-specific fixture helper over a generic read.

`node:module` -- and therefore `createRequire` -- is a generic module-loader capability: it resolves and loads arbitrary paths, which is the same capability as `fs` reached by another route. It is available only to the exact package-resolution exceptions in the reader ledger, which may resolve DECLARED package ids and must not hand a generic loader back to their callers. WHICH MECHANISM OWNS WHAT: this rule owns every literal specifier, STATIC AND DYNAMIC ALIKE -- a probe on the installed Oxlint 1.74 shows `await import("node:module")` rejected here, so ast-grep deliberately does NOT match `import()` and adding a rule for it would duplicate this one. The residual shapes ast-grep owns are the ones no specifier appears in: `require()`, a `createRequire` CALL (including a locally-named loader handle), and `process.getBuiltinModule()`.

zundo's temporal handle is retired along with the middleware itself. Reversal availability comes from the committed envelope through the authority projection (canUndo / canRedo), which is the same answer in every tab.

paths.name: @copilotkit/react-core
paths.message: The legacy root entry point is restricted WHOLE: it exports executable registrants (useFrontendTool, useHumanInTheLoop, useCopilotAction, useDefaultTool, useCopilotAuthenticatedAction_c), the legacy action registry (CopilotContext, useCopilotContext), an executable task runner (CopilotTask), a HITL resume handler (useLangGraphInterrupt) and the legacy provider (CopilotKit) -- and it re-exports more through wildcards. Production imports nothing from it, so the whole specifier is closed rather than enumerated. Use components/ai/register-model-visible-tool.ts, copilotkit-core-access.ts and assistant-copilot-provider.tsx.

paths.name: @copilotkit/react-core/v2
paths.message: Each of these executes or resumes a model-callable handler, or yields a core that can register one -- including CopilotKitCore and RunHandler, which reach this specifier through its `export * from "@copilotkit/core"` wildcard and expose addTool/removeTool/setTools/setToolEnabled/runTool. Register through useModelVisibleTool, obtain per-turn runtime through copilotkit-core-access.ts, and mount the provider through assistant-copilot-provider.tsx. Renderer-only hooks (useRenderTool, useRenderToolCall, useDefaultRenderTool, defineToolCallRenderer) are deliberately NOT restricted: they add a ReactToolCallRenderer and cannot register, replace or respond with an executable result.

paths.name: @copilotkit/react-core/v2/context
paths.message: This subpath publicly exports useCopilotKit, CopilotKitContext and the CopilotKitCoreReact class, so any of them yields the live mutable core. Read core configuration through components/ai/copilotkit-core-access.ts instead. The whole specifier is restricted because every one of its exports is a route to the same capability.

paths.name: @copilotkit/react-core/v2/headless
paths.message: The headless entry point is restricted WHOLE: it exports executable registrants (useFrontendTool, useHumanInTheLoop, useComponent), a HITL resume handler (useInterrupt), core access (useCopilotKit, CopilotKitCoreReact) and the same `export *` wildcards as /v2, which carry CopilotKitCore and RunHandler. Production imports nothing from it, so the whole specifier is closed rather than enumerated.

paths.name: zundo
paths.message: The temporal middleware is retired. Undo/redo is a durable repository operation (scenarioCommands.undo/redo) whose availability is read from the committed envelope, not a per-tab in-memory stack that lies across tabs.

paths.name: zustand/middleware
paths.message: The scenario projection is no longer a persist-wrapped store. Durable writes go through the repository transaction and are PUBLISHED into the projection afterwards; a write-behind would put the view ahead of the commit again, which is the exact failure the T03 cutover removed.

paths.name: lucide-react
paths.message: The project standardizes on react-icons Font Awesome 6 (react-icons/fa6), re-exported through components/icons.tsx. lucide-react arrives as a transitive shadcn/base-nova dependency and is not this app's icon set: importing it would put two icon families -- two stroke weights, two optical sizes -- on the same screen. Migrated here from the recursive app/ + components/ source walk in app/design-system.test.ts, which is exactly the job no-restricted-imports already does natively.

paths.name: @copilotkit/react-core/v2/styles.css
paths.message: The CopilotKit v2 stylesheet is a PRODUCTION CSS ENTRY and there is exactly one: `app/layout.tsx`, which imports it before `./globals.css` so the token mapping in globals.css can re-point the library's scoped theme. A second entry double-ships ~87KB and, if it lands after globals.css, silently undoes that mapping and returns the dock to the library's pure-white / near-black defaults. This restriction replaces the recursive app/ + components/ import walk that components/ai/assistant-styles.test.ts used to run: closing the specifier makes a second entry UNAVAILABLE rather than merely unspelled, and unlike the walk it covers aliases, re-export chains and dynamic import() in every directory. Whether the sheet is actually shipped and ACTIVE is owned by e2e/ai-assistant-chat-ui.spec.ts against a real production build.

patterns.message: The CopilotKit RUNTIME is reachable only through lib/ai/runtime/copilotkit-runtime.ts, which applies the telemetry/analytics containment env before the package's telemetry singleton snapshots it. Importing the package anywhere else boots an uncontained runtime and breaks the single-instance identity Phase 1 depends on.

The durable repository is reached only by the projection adapter (lib/store/authority.ts) and the explicitly listed modules that own their own tables or the write fence. Everything else changes durable scenario state through scenarioCommands / assistantProposalCommands, so a failed write can never leave the view showing something that was not saved.
Same boundary as the aliased specifier: a RELATIVE path into lib/repository is the same crossing. This regex is why the boundary is not merely a spelling rule about `@/lib/repository`.

AI IS OPTIONAL. With the feature off, no key stored, or OpenRouter unreachable, every manual workflow and ordinary Optimize keeps working -- and what guarantees that is that no scheduling code DEPENDS on assistant code. The assistant's modules may be imported by itself, its UI, the settings card, the two shell surfaces that mount it (both render null until it is Ready), the same-origin AI routes, and the boot instrumentation. Every one of those is listed by name in an override, because a new entry is a deliberate widening of the seam.
Same boundary, relative spelling: a path into lib/ai or components/ai crosses it whichever way it is written.

People and Shift Types are bespoke screens over components/entity-editor/core; the shared substrate (core, groups-section, transfer-list, working-time-fields) is deliberately NOT matched. The module does not exist, so the compiler already refuses this import -- this rule is what makes the refusal say why.

Test and support code may not acquire a compiler or parser library. Every guarantee that used to be proved by parsing authored source now sits at the first layer that can own it honestly: a production API, a TypeScript option or negative fixture, an Oxlint restriction, a runtime/behavioural test, or a declarative ast-grep rule with its own valid/invalid fixtures. THIS FAMILY HAS NO AUDITED EXCEPTION ANYWHERE -- if a guarantee appears to need a parser, the answer is to change the production API, not to import one here. This rule owns every literal specifier for these packages, static and dynamic alike; ast-grep owns only the residual `require()` / `createRequire` / `getBuiltinModule` call shapes, in which no specifier appears for an import rule to see.

`node:module` -- and therefore `createRequire` -- is a generic module-loader capability: it resolves and loads arbitrary paths, which is the same capability as `fs` reached by another route. It is available only to the exact package-resolution exceptions in the reader ledger, which may resolve DECLARED package ids and must not hand a generic loader back to their callers. WHICH MECHANISM OWNS WHAT: this rule owns every literal specifier, STATIC AND DYNAMIC ALIKE -- a probe on the installed Oxlint 1.74 shows `await import("node:module")` rejected here, so ast-grep deliberately does NOT match `import()` and adding a rule for it would duplicate this one. The residual shapes ast-grep owns are the ones no specifier appears in: `require()`, a `createRequire` CALL (including a locally-named loader handle), and `process.getBuiltinModule()`.
